title: Grouping and Conditional Execution knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Grouping and Conditional Execution”?
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Command grouping with braces” under lesson 59, “Grouping and Conditional Execution”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Grouping and Conditional Execution”?
options: Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
Test commands directly and make loop termination and default branches explicit.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
questions.answer_key: Test commands directly and make loop termination and default branches explicit.
questions.explanation: Test commands directly and make loop termination and default branches explicit. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Grouping and Conditional Execution”?
options: Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
questions.answer_key: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
questions.explanation: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
